npcs.name: Warden Osric Ashby
greeting: A stranger, and at this hour. Well. Those I knew are dead or under suspicion, so you are welcome.
Keep out of the Tower after dark and we shall get on.

talk.label: What happened here?
lines: Eleven nights gone the king was slain in his own tower, poisoned first and then stabbed, and the Crown taken from its stand.
We found a white mask upon the floor, smooth, with the eyeholes sealed. Make of that what you will. I have made nothing of it yet.

talk.label: Who are you?
lines: Osric Ashby. I led the guard thirty years, and I lead what is left of it still.
It is not many. That is why I am speaking to you.

npcs.name: Sergeant Maud Cotterill
greeting: Stand up straight. Hold that sword like you mean it.
The yard is yours when you want it. The monsters in the Reach are for after.

talk.label: Tell me about fighting.
lines: One level for everything. You earn points as you climb and spend them in the skill tree, press K. Swords, bows, staves, shields: any of them can carry you the whole way.
A shield in your off hand opens the Defense tree and takes a flat slice off every blow. Wear one even if you fight from a distance.

talk.label: Can I hire a sword?
lines: Not yet. Contracts for sellswords, archers, and hedge mages are being drawn up. Come back when the clerks are done arguing.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Nan Whitlow
greeting: Armor is cheaper than a funeral. Look around.

talk.label: About the gear
lines: Leather for the quick, chain for the stubborn. Tier two needs level 10 to wear, tier three needs 20. I do not sell moonsilver. Nobody does.

npcs.name: Denis Rudge
greeting: Welcome to the Storage. Everything you leave is yours alone, and it stays in every town you visit.

talk.label: How does it work?
lines: You have 120 places to set things down. The Crown Steward can sell you more. Put gear and spare ore in, take it out anywhere there is a storage keeper.
I also change coin. A hundred iron bits for one gold coin, and the same back. No fee. I am not that sort of man.

npcs.name: Harold Tibbs
greeting: Rope, bread, axes, anything. If I do not have it, you do not need it.

talk.label: Where do I start?
lines: Buy an axe, a pickaxe, a rod, and a snare. Chop pine west of the wall, dig copper and tin at the Old Quarry east of it, fish the pond south, and snare rabbits in the meadow beyond.
Cook what you catch at the range in the Gilt Dog. Smelt and forge at Hadley. Craft at the hall. Sell me what you do not need. I pay forty percent. It is not personal.

npcs.name: Tom Hadley
greeting: Mind the sparks. Bronze today, steel when you have earned it.

talk.label: How do I smith?
lines: Smelt at the furnace: one copper and one tin make a bronze bar. Then the anvil. Daggers take a bar, swords take two. The higher the tier, the higher your Smithing level has to be: 1, 10, 20, 30.

talk.label: Do you know Gimrik?
lines: Old Gimrik Ironvein? Every smith knows Gimrik. He will not forge what he is not proud of. I forge it anyway and sleep fine.

npcs.name: Joan Sewell
greeting: Come in, come in. Do not sit on the bench, it is not finished.

talk.label: What can I make here?
lines: At the bench: bows and staves from logs, and armor from hides. Two logs make a bow. Four hides make a jerkin. Snare rabbits for soft leather.
The levels match the gear tiers. Level 10 for iron-grade, 20 and 30 beyond.

npcs.name: Bert Oakley
greeting: A bed, a bowl, or both? The range is free for guests.

talk.label: The name of the inn?
lines: The Gilt Dog. The hound was a real hound. The gold was the king's idea of a joke. He drank here once, before the Tower got his attention.

npcs.name: Hal the Piper
greeting: A song for a bit? Fine. A song for nothing? Even better.

talk.label: Sing something.
lines: "In the days when the Welling was young, and men feared it not,
the bells of Aldmoor rang at dusk to call the wanderers home."
That is as far as I got. The rest is in Gullsend, and I am not going to Gullsend.

talk.label: Sing something real.
lines: "The wind doth blow today, my love, and a few small drops of rain;
I never had but one true-love, in cold grave she was lain."
"I'll do as much for my true-love as any young man may;
I'll sit and mourn all at her grave for a twelvemonth and a day."
"The twelvemonth and a day being up, the dead began to speak:
'Oh who sits weeping on my grave, and will not let me sleep?'"
My grandmother's song. Nobody knows who made it. She said that is why it lasted.

talk.label: Heard any rumors?
lines: The cook in the Tower swears her stew was clean. The stable boy swears a masked figure left by night. The guard swears at everyone.
I would ask Tam. He sees more than he says.

npcs.name: Magister Edith Crane
greeting: Magic is a craft, not a gift. You, however, look like you have a little of both.

talk.label: Explain the skill trees.
lines: There are four: Melee, Range, Magic, Defense. You earn points with every level, five a level up to fifty. Spend them where you like. Rows open at levels 8, 16, 24, 32, and 40.
Skills joined to one another feed each other: three percent more damage for every rank in the skill above. All four trees can carry you through any content if you commit to one.

talk.label: Is the Academy still open?
lines: It is open. The king funded half of it, so we are open for as long as the chancellor can find the other half.

talk.label: What are the teleport anchors?
lines: Anchors are old waystones set at the places travellers actually go. Stand beside one and it will learn you.
The early ones cost nothing. The Plaza, the Warren gate, the Quarry camp and Dunhollow are free, to make the first leagues kinder.

The rest need a Teleport Crystal, fifteen gold apiece. I do not set the price lightly. Each one is cut by hand and tuned to a single stone. Once an anchor is attuned, you may travel between any two you have attuned, as often as you like, for nothing.

npcs.name: Initiate Davy
greeting: I am supposed to be copying runes. Do not tell the Magister you saw me.

talk.label: What do you study?
lines: Welling. The thing under everything. It leaks upward and makes wolves cast two shadows. Nobody knows why. I am going to find out and then I am going to be famous.

npcs.name: Lord Steward Aubrey Pryce
greeting: The Crown has no king and the Tower has a steward. That is the arrangement.
Deeds earn the realm's favor. I trade in it.

talk.label: What is favor?
lines: Tokens of the realm's thanks. You earn them for deeds, never for coin. They cannot be traded or sold, which is the point.
I can give you a title to wear or more room in the Storage.

npcs.name: Crown Guard Ruth Tanner
greeting: No one goes up. Warden's orders. Not even you.

talk.label: What did you see that night?
lines: Nothing. I was on the east stair. That is the whole problem. Every guard that night was on the wrong stair.

npcs.name: Tam
greeting: I did not take the mare. I did not.

talk.label: You saw something?
lines: I saw a tall man in a pale mask go out by the west gate on Harvest Eve. He did not walk like a man. He walked like water poured out of a jug.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Hob Gedney
greeting: Gate is open, gate is mended, gate is mine. Mostly.

talk.label: Anything out there?
lines: Moss imps close to the wall, glowcap crawlers farther out. Gnashers beyond that, and they come in packs. If a gnasher looks at you, you are already late.

npcs.name: Fred the Crier
greeting: Hear ye! Hear... oh, it is just you.

talk.label: The news?
lines: The Warden asks the city to stay calm. The Academy asks the city to stay out of its cellar. The innkeeper asks the city to stop using the word "haunted".

talk.label: Controls?
lines: Click the ground to walk, click a person to speak, click a tree or a rock to work it. K skills, I bag, E gear, C stats, J journal. Press M for the whole map.

npcs.name: Sam Lacey
greeting: I am nineteen. Do not look at me like that. I am nineteen.

talk.label: Know anything?
lines: I know that a pie vendor on Cobbler Row has a bag with a hole in it, and that guard Ruth is afraid of cats. I also know the Tower has a second stair. Do not tell the Warden I said.

npcs.name: Meg Hollis
greeting: Pines are good wood. Soft, quick, forgiving. Like me.

talk.label: Tips on forestry?
lines: Pine opens at level 1. Birch at 10, oak at 20, willow at 30. A pine you cut may or may not fall; if it does, it grows back in under a minute. Take your time, there are plenty.

npcs.name: Dick Aston
greeting: Copper and tin, both here, both for the taking. The wall keeps the quarry quiet.

talk.label: Tips on mining?
lines: Dig copper and tin, bring them to a furnace. Both ores are level 1. Iron is level 10, but it is not here. Dunhollow has the iron. Go there when you can bear to be stared at by tired people.

npcs.name: Old Barnaby
greeting: Quiet. They hear you.

talk.label: Tips on fishing?
lines: Shrimp in the pond shallows. Level 1, easy. Trout at 10 is in Longmere. Cook your catch. A raw shrimp is a fine lesson in regret.

npcs.name: Kit Ferris
greeting: Shh. Rabbits.

talk.label: Tips on hunting?
lines: Set a snare at a warren. You get a pelt and sometimes meat. Pelts are soft leather, and soft leather is armor if you take it to the Crafters' Hall.

npcs.name: Mabel Cheney
greeting: Mind the gate, love. The hens get out.

talk.label: What do you grow here?
lines: Barley, mostly, and a little flax. The hay goes to the quarry mules. Bread for the city comes from my oven, and you can buy it at the general store, so you need not pay my prices.

talk.label: Any trouble out here?
lines: Moss imps in the hedge, now and then. The goblins up by the pines keep to themselves, which is more than I can say for their pine nuts. I find them in the hen house.

npcs.name: Nell Garrick
greeting: Keep your voice down. The warren is right there.

talk.label: What is in the warren?
lines: Goblins, a lot of them. Pinegrubs up front, nutcrackers behind them with the big clubs. They eat pine nuts all day and they are never short of any.

talk.label: Who leads them?
lines: The Mind Goblin. Big as a cart, ugly as a boiled boot, and he throws pine nuts at you from across the room. It sounds funny until the third one lands.
Go in with food and a full bag. You cannot run from him once the fight starts.

npcs.name: Hetty Bloom
greeting: Beds are six bits. The soup is free if you do not ask what is in it.

talk.label: What is the village like?
lines: Dunhollow lives on iron. The Foreman Marrow keeps the shifts, Peg buys the ore, Ray makes it into something. The mine under the hill is the reason we are here and the reason half of us do not sleep.

npcs.name: Walt Bayliss
greeting: Same storage as every town. What you leave in Aldmoor you can take out here.

talk.label: Is it safe?
lines: Safer than the rest of the Downs. Nothing has taken from this room in thirty years, and I count the shelves every night.

npcs.name: Foreman Edna Marrow
greeting: If you are here for work, wait your turn. If you are here to complain, wait longer.

talk.label: What is the Delve?
lines: The mine under the hill, the Black Sump. It flooded eleven weeks ago, in the night. The second shift was below. We have not heard from them since.
The man who ran that shift was my brother. I would like to know what happened to him before anyone else tells me.

talk.label: Who was the last foreman?
lines: I am the only foreman Dunhollow has. Ask me again when the Delve is quiet.

npcs.name: Peg Dunmore
greeting: I buy ore at fair weight and sell picks at a fair price. Do not weigh your thumb.

talk.label: Any trouble?
lines: Rats. They come up out of the Delve through the drains and eat the sacks. I would pay for the lot of them.

npcs.name: Ray Stokes
greeting: The furnace is lit. Anvil is free. Do not stand there and talk.

talk.label: How do I smelt iron?
lines: One ore, one bar, at the furnace. Smithing level 10. Then bars go to the anvil for blades and daggers. Coal and iron together make steel, at level 20.

npcs.name: Wilf Barrett
greeting: Mind the pen. The ewes bite.

talk.label: What do you keep?
lines: Forty ewes, a ram, and a dog who thinks the ram is his. The Downs grass is good. The boars are not.

talk.label: Seen anything odd?
lines: The bats come out of the Delve at dusk, in a cloud. They used to come back before dawn. Now they stay out.

npcs.name: Lenny Reeve
greeting: I am not leaving. Not until my crew is out of there.

talk.label: Why are you here?
lines: I was on the second shift. I came up for a break and the water came down the main shaft behind me. I have sat at this door every day since.

talk.label: What is down there?
lines: Rats, bats, wretches that were my friends, boars that came in through the broken wall. And at the bottom, the Foreman. The old foreman. Edna Marrow's brother. He still gives orders. He does not give them to people.

npcs.name: Reeve Ivy Penn
greeting: You are the one who came up the south road. I am Ivy Penn. I keep newcomers out of the Sump and out of trouble.
Ask me whatever you like. Everyone does, the first morning.

talk.label: How do I get around?
lines: Click the ground to walk. Scroll or press plus and minus to zoom, and M shows the whole map.
Click a person to talk to them, or a tree, rock or pond to work it. Hold the mouse over anything and a small card tells you what it is.

talk.label: How does fighting work?
lines: Click a monster to start a fight. It plays out in turns on a grid. Move on the blue tiles, pick an ability from the bar, then click your target.
Your weapon sets your reach. Blades and daggers fight up close, a bow reaches six tiles and a staff five. If it goes badly you can flee, though the monsters stay angry for a moment.

talk.label: What is hit chance?
lines: A weapon swing lands about three times in four against a foe your own level. A higher skill or accuracy gear improves it, and a tougher foe lowers it. It never falls below one in twenty.
Spells never miss, unless something has blinded you. Open your stats with C to see your own number.

talk.label: Skills, gear and bag
lines: K opens your skills, where you spend a point each time you level. I is your bag, E is what you wear, and C shows your stats.
Better gear comes from drops, from the smith, and from the shops. Rare and legendary pieces carry powers of their own.

talk.label: Gathering and crafting
lines: Chop trees, mine rock, fish the pond and snare rabbits. Pine is level one, birch ten, oak twenty and willow thirty. Dark-green narrow trees are pines, pale trunks are birch.
Take what you gather to the smith and the cook. They turn it into gear and food.

talk.label: Portals, checkpoints and signing out
lines: Press T to cast the town portal. It takes a few breaths, you have to stand still, and it will not work in a fight. It carries you to your last checkpoint.
Walk into a safe place near a bellstone or a town gate and it becomes your checkpoint. That is where you wake after a fall or a sign-out.
One warning. Sign out in the middle of a fight inside a dungeon and you lose what that delve gave you.

talk.label: Where should I start?
lines: Warden Osric stands by the Crown Tower, north of here. He wants a stranger with fresh eyes. His first errand is easy.
Tam at the stable has moss imps chewing his harness, south of the gate. Clear three and you will have earned a hearing.

npcs.name: Tess Gale
greeting: Mind the rope on the floor. The fog gets in everywhere and brings the damp with it.
Beds are eight bits. The fish is good. Ask nothing about the cellar.

talk.label: What is Gullsend like?
lines: Fog, rope and tar. We are a fishing town. That is the story and we all keep to it.
The old families come in on the first of the month, drink one cup each, and leave before the tide turns. I pour. I do not listen.

talk.label: The harbor bells
lines: They ring when a certain kind of boat comes in. No, I will not say which kind.

npcs.name: Aelwyn
greeting: If you are here to tell me who I am, do not. I have heard it. Twice today.
I am carrying plates. Plates do not ask questions.

talk.label: You look like someone I have seen.
lines: Everyone says that. It is the nose. Please stop looking at my nose.

talk.label: Do you want to leave?
lines: I want to hit something. A lot. The boars in the dunes would do. They do not look at my face.

npcs.name: Harbormaster Eli Trevick
greeting: Every boat that ties up here, I know. Every boat that does not, I also know. Fishing licence is free. Honesty is extra.

talk.label: How is the harbor?
lines: Busy for a fishing port. We land a lot of cargo for a place that lands so few fish. I keep my ledger tidy and my eyes on the ledger.

talk.label: Where do I fish?
lines: Piers out to the south. Trout near the shore, level ten. Salmon farther out, level twenty. Tuna at the pier heads, thirty. You will want a better rod each time. Dan sells them.

npcs.name: Dan Marlow
greeting: Nets, rods, hooks, bait. If it can be caught I sell something that catches it.

talk.label: Which rod?
lines: Ash for trout. Oak for salmon. For tuna you want a lantern rod, and I cannot sell you one. The only ones I have seen came out of the water on their own.

npcs.name: Bill Hale
greeting: Use the range. Cook your own, or buy mine. Raw fish makes poor friends.

talk.label: What should I cook?
lines: Trout at ten. Salmon at twenty. Tuna at thirty, and take it off the heat early or it turns to rope. A cooked fish heals more than any bread.

npcs.name: Dame Rhoda Quill
greeting: Draw to the ear. Loose on the breath. Anyone who tells you different has not hit anything.

talk.label: Teach me.
lines: A bow reaches six tiles, so you fight with space. Stay at the edge of their reach and keep moving. Anything that closes on you, you have already lost the exchange.
Buy a birch bow before you buy anything else. Then go and shoot gnashers on the road until you stop flinching.

npcs.name: Mick Quist
greeting: You are not from the families. Good. That means you will listen to me and then forget me.

talk.label: What do the families do?
lines: They land things at night. Crates with no marks. Men who do not give names. Sometimes they ask the harbor bells to ring twice and the tide to go out early.

talk.label: The Wan Company
lines: I never said that word. I said a man in a white mask paid for my silence. I took it. Whoever asks next gets the same story.

npcs.name: Gil Rudd
greeting: Snares, nets, pits. If it walks, I can make it stop.

talk.label: What traps work?
lines: Rope snares for small game. Net traps for wolves, and they are not enough. Pit traps hold anything that is not clever. The pack-lord is clever.

npcs.name: Warden Leofric
greeting: You have the look of someone who finishes things. Good. I have a pack that needs finishing.

talk.label: What is wrong with the wolves?
lines: Someone is feeding them meat that has been in the ground. It does not rot. It makes them hungry, and then it makes them worse.
The trail runs to the Nameless Cairns. I have not gone in. I am not proud of that.

npcs.name: Harry Brack
greeting: Oak for the road, willow for the long shot. Ask me about draw weights and I will not stop.

talk.label: Which bow?
lines: Oak for most. Willow if you have the coin and the shoulders. Either way, do not shoot a wight. Fire and blunt, as the saying goes.

npcs.name: Dot Fell
greeting: Venison, smoked slow. Do not ask what kind of wood. The wood is none of your business.

talk.label: Any news?
lines: The Warden has been quiet for a week. When the Warden is quiet, someone is about to be sent somewhere.

npcs.name: Olive Reed
greeting: Lanterns stay lit all night. Do not ask why. The fish ask often enough.
Beds are twelve bits. The water is cold. The soup is not.

talk.label: Why the lanterns?
lines: Something down there follows the light. As long as it follows ours, it does not follow you home.

talk.label: Tell me about Marwick.
lines: We live on stilts because the ground is not trusted here. The lake gives fish and takes the odd boat. We call it even.

npcs.name: Toby Larkin
greeting: Rods, nets, floats. If it swims, I sell something that catches it.

talk.label: The eels?
lines: They came up from the old hall in the spring. They bite through nets and now they bite through boots. Someone should thin them.

npcs.name: Moll Lowe
greeting: I trim the lamps and watch the water. The water has started watching back.

talk.label: What is under the lake?
lines: A hall. No one built it. The architecture has more angles than it should, and the water that fills it does not come from the lake.
The fish glow the wrong color now. Coins turn up in the nets. Old ones, with a face on them nobody remembers.

npcs.name: Gwen Pike
greeting: Fish stew, fish pie, fried fish. Do not ask for anything else.

talk.label: Any advice?
lines: Cook salmon over the range for as long as it takes to say a short prayer. Then eat it before the lake changes its mind.

npcs.name: Nick the Hermit
greeting: You found me. Nobody finds me. I have been practising.
Sit. Mind the goat. The goat is not mine.

talk.label: Why live out here?
lines: The Welling is quieter at the edge of the map. Or it was. Lately the hum has a tune in it, and I find I know the words.

talk.label: Do you know the Crown?
lines: Only that it is not asleep. It waits, and a thing that waits is listening.
Gather what you must. But when you hold all five Seals, say nothing until you are certain of the word.

talk.label: Who wrote the notes?
lines: A scholar called Quaile came through in the spring, asking about the Seals. He walked on toward the lake and did not walk back.
If you find his pages, read them in order. He got cleverer with each one, and then he got careful.

stations.name: The empty stand
text: A cushion of red velvet on a plinth of white stone. The dent where the Crown sat is still there.
Someone has swept the stairs, but a little black ash is caught in the grain of the step.

stations.name: Notice board
text: WANTED: strong backs to fell pine for the gate. Ask Hob at the south gate.
LOST: one brown mare. Do not ask Tam where. He knows.
The Warden asks that no one go into the Crown Tower after dark. No reason is given.
Smiths pay good bits for bronze bars. Copper and tin lie in the Old Quarry, east of the wall.

stations.name: Signpost
text: North road: the Mossgate Reach ends at the treeline. Nothing past it has been charted. South: Aldmoor, one hour.

stations.name: Signpost
text: South road. West: Rabbit Meadow and the trapper's cabin. East: Mere Pool and the angler's dock. Straight on: the Tumbledown Watch.

stations.name: Signpost
text: West road. The Whispering Pines and the woodcutter's lodge lie ahead. The Goblin Warren is north of the pines. Go with food.

stations.name: Signpost
text: East road. The bridge over Silverrun Creek is just ahead. Beyond it: the Old Quarry and Hollow Farm.

stations.name: Warning sign
text: GOBLIN WARREN. Pinegrubs and nutcrackers inside, and something larger at the back. Once the big one has you, you cannot run. Four people went in this season and three came back.

stations.name: Signpost
text: Mere Pool. Shrimp in the shallows. The dock is for anglers; the lamp is Marl's and he will know if you move it.

stations.name: Signpost
text: Old Quarry. Copper and tin for any back strong enough. Dick buys ore at fair weight.

stations.name: Signpost
text: Hollow Farm. Follow the lane south. Shut the field gate behind you.

stations.name: Signpost
text: Tumbledown Watch. A guard post from before the walls. It fell down before anyone now living was born. Mind the stones.

stations.name: Carved stone
text: A worn block in the middle of the ruin, with a ring of letters round the edge. The weather has taken most of them.
What is left reads: HERE THE WATCH KEPT THE ROAD. Someone has scratched underneath it: and then it did not.

stations.name: Notice board
text: WANTED: hands for the Drainage Cut. Marrow pays in iron bits. Bring birch logs and iron ore to the office.
REWARD: any word of the second shift. Six went down the Delve and did not come up. Ask Lenny at the mouth.
Sump rats in the ore store again. Peg will pay a bounty. She does not say how much.
Smith wants iron bars. Smelt them at the furnace. Smithing level 10.

stations.name: Signal beacon stone
text: A blackened stone basin on the floor of the ruined tower, where the signal fire burned. It has not burned for a long time.
A rope has been tied to the rim and run out through the gap in the wall, toward the Delve. The knot is a miner's knot.

stations.name: Signpost
text: South road to Dunhollow. The Downs are open ground: sump rats, cave bats, and boars that do not wait to be asked. The old signal tower is east, off the road.

stations.name: Signpost
text: Dunhollow, one furlong. A mining village. The inn has beds, the office has work, and the smith will buy your bars.

stations.name: Signpost
text: Ironback Rocks. Iron for a level 10 pick, coal for a better one. Keep your back to the wall when the boars come down from the hill.

stations.name: Warning sign
text: DELVE OF THE BLACK SUMP. Flooded workings. Do not go in alone. Rats in the first galleries, bats in the east cave, wretches in the pools. At the bottom, the Foreman. You cannot run from him.

stations.name: Old well
text: The water is cold and hums a little at night. Everyone in Aldmoor has stopped noticing.
Lean over the rim long enough and the hum begins to sound like your own name.

stations.name: Trade board
text: WANTED: strong lines and steady hands at the piers. The harbormaster pays for trout, a lot of trout.
NO QUESTIONS ASKED, NO QUESTIONS ANSWERED. Inquire at the Gull's Rest. (Someone has crossed this out. Someone else has written it again.)
The best trade board in the realm, they say. Look closely at the cargo lists. The weights never add up.

stations.name: Signpost
text: COAST ROAD. West along the cut, then south to Gullsend. Far. Take food.

stations.name: Signpost
text: INNSHARROW. Port city. Tavern, quay, piers. Dunes to the east, marsh to the west. Keep to the road after dark.

stations.name: Signpost
text: MARSH. Wretches in the shallows. Not a place to walk with a full pack.

stations.name: Signpost
text: THE DUNES. Boars root in the sand. They hit harder than they look.

stations.name: Hunters' board
text: WANTED: wolves, dead. Pelts paid by the Warden. Heads not wanted.
FOR SALE: one very good bow, one careful owner. Inquire at the Bowyer.
WARNING: do not feed the pack. Do not feed anything. (Someone has written "too late" under this.)

stations.name: Signpost
text: MARSH CAUSEWAY. South shore road to Wargwatch. Keep to the planks. The tide comes in quickly.

stations.name: Signpost
text: WARGWATCH. Hunters' lodge, trapper, bowyer, smokehouse. The mounds are not for climbing.

stations.name: Signpost
text: THE NAMELESS CAIRNS. Nobody carved the names. Do not carve yours.

stations.name: Village board
text: WANTED: steady hands for the lamps. Bring your own oil.
NOTICE: coins in your net belong to the lake. Return them. (Someone has written "they do not want them back".)
LOST: one boat, one dog. The dog came back.

stations.name: Signpost
text: NAERWICK. Stilt village on Longmere. Walk the planks. Lanterns burn all night.

stations.name: Signpost
text: THE DROWNED HALL. No one built it. No one has come back to say who did.

stations.name: Signpost
text: LAKE ROAD. South along the shore, then east to Marwick. The marsh is not safe after dark.

stations.name: Teleport anchor
text: A waystone humming with a faint blue light. Stand beside it to attune it and travel to other anchors.

stations.name: Small gravestone
text: HERE LIES SIR ALWIN PETTIGREW. HE FEARED NOTHING IN THE WEALDMARK.
Underneath, in smaller letters: and then there was the hen. A second, tinier stone beside it reads: THE HEN. AVENGED.

stations.name: Scrap of paper
text: A page torn from a notebook and held down with a pebble. "First day out of Aldmoor. The streams here hum at night, and I find I hum with them. My landlady says it is only the Welling and I should mind my feet. H. Quaile."

stations.name: Pie on a rock
text: A pie cooling on a flat rock, with a note: FOR THE ONE WHO LOOKS. It is still warm, and nobody is anywhere near.
You decide not to eat it. Then you decide that you will, and find that you cannot pick it up. Some pies can only be admired.

stations.name: Rod in a boulder
text: A fishing rod stuck fast in a boulder. A sign reads: WHOEVER PULLS THIS FREE SHALL BE KING OF THE WEALDMARK.
Beneath, in a tired hand: please do not. The queue is already long.

stations.name: Whispering stone
text: You put your ear to the stone. Faintly, a piper's tune: half a verse, over and over. Then a voice, quite close, says: "No. Gullsend is that way."

stations.name: Scrap of paper
text: A page folded small and wedged in a crack. "Dunhollow. The miners say the Black Sump took its name from the water, and the water took its color from something else. I asked to be taken below. They laughed, and then they stopped. H. Quaile."

stations.name: Carved fence post
text: A fence post with DEREK carved into it in very large letters. A smaller scratch beneath: the ram is called Derek. the dog disagrees.

stations.name: Loose stone
text: Behind a loose stone, a miner's lunch tin. Inside are a pasty gone hard as slate and a scrap of paper: "If I do not come up, Edna gets my good pick. Gaz."
The pasty is not part of the bequest.

stations.name: Bottle in the reeds
text: A bottle washed up among the reeds. Inside, a note: HELP, I AM STUCK IN A BOTTLE.
The bottle is empty. The note is very pleased with itself.

stations.name: Small harbor bell
text: A bell on a post, its clapper muffled in sacking. Scratched into the bronze: once for the tide, twice for the families, thrice for the Company.
The sacking looks new.

stations.name: Scrap of paper
text: A page in bottle-green ink. "The Cairns bear no names. Someone has been at the stones with a chisel, and not so very long ago. One does not scrape a grave unless one fears what it says. H. Quaile."

stations.name: Neat woodpile
text: A woodpile, very tidy, with a tiny carved wolf on top no bigger than a thumb. Warden Leofric will deny it.
The hunters call him Softpaws behind his back.

stations.name: Unscraped stone
text: One stone in the Cairns was missed by the chisel, or spared. The letters are small and deep: HERE ELDRED DID NOT WISH TO BE FOUND.

Below, in a newer hand: "Five Seals, and the name is one word broken five ways. I have the sum of it in my head and I dare not say it aloud. The Crown cannot be named by one hand, only by all. H. Quaile."

stations.name: Chalk slate
text: A slate nailed to a post, crowded with chalk tallies. At the bottom, in another hand: "Lamps lit tonight: 4,018. Lamps seen below the water: 4,019."

stations.name: Scrap of paper
text: A page stuck to a post with fish glue. "Marwick. I have drawn the Hall as well as I can, but the angles will not stay drawn. The lamp-keeper says the lake counts the lamps. I begin to think it counts us too. H. Quaile."

stations.name: Hollow under the stones
text: A hollow lined with apples, each one marked in charcoal: NOT SAM'S.

quests.name: The Empty Stand
quests.summary: The king is dead and the Crown is gone. Osric wants a stranger with fresh eyes.
offer: The Crown lay on a stand in the Tower. Look at it if you like; the guard on the door will let you stand outside, no further.
Before that, go to the stable and talk to Tam. He saw something that night and he is too frightened to say what.
Be kind to him. He is twelve and thinks he is in trouble.

steps.todo: Ask Tam what he saw. He wants three moss imps driven off the road first.
say: The harness is safe again. Thank you.
waiting: I will tell you what I saw. But the imps keep chewing the harness. Drive off three, outside the wall, and I will tell you everything. They are south of the gate, among the trees.

steps.todo: Hear what Tam saw.
say: A tall man in a pale mask walked out by the west gate on Harvest Eve. He did not walk like a man. He walked like water poured out of a jug.
Tell the Warden. Tell him I did not take the mare.

steps.todo: Tell Osric about the masked man.
say: The west gate. Of course. They went the long way round, so no guard would see.
You have done more in an afternoon than my whole watch did in eleven days. Take this. It is not much, but you will need the tools.

done: Osric looks at the west gate for a long time, then back at you.
"Good work, Wanderer. Come back when you have more of the Reach in your boots."

quests.name: The First Lesson
quests.summary: Magister Edith wants to see you spend your first skill point.
offer: You have points to spend already. Open the tree with K and put one into anything. A hero with unspent points is a hero who is not trying.

steps.todo: Open the skill tree (K) and spend a point, then return to the Magister.
waiting: You have not spent a point yet. Press K.

done: "Good. Now you know how it feels. Every rank counts, and you can take them all back for a fee if you change your mind."
She nods, once, the way teachers do when you have not embarrassed them.

quests.name: Timber for the Gate
quests.summary: Hob needs pine to mend the south gate.
offer: The south gate has not been mended since before the war. Ten pine logs, cut and clean. I will pay you out of my own pocket, which is a sentence I have never said.

steps.todo: Bring Hob 10 pine logs (Forestry).
waiting: Ten pine logs. Meg Hollis is in the grove west of the wall. Chop a tree, it takes a few swings.

done: Hob takes the logs, counts them twice, and counts them a third time on principle.
"Honest weight. Fine work."

quests.name: Copper and Tin
quests.summary: Hadley needs bronze bars for the guard.
offer: The guard wants new buckles and I am out of bronze. Three bars. Copper and tin from the Old Quarry, smelt them at my furnace, a bar each.
Do it yourself. I will not pay for work I could do faster myself.

steps.todo: Bring Hadley 3 bronze bars (Mining and Smithing).
waiting: Three bronze bars. One copper and one tin each. The furnace is behind me.

done: Hadley turns a bar over, sniffs it, and nods.
"Clean smelt. You might be a smith yet."

quests.name: Supper for the Watch
quests.summary: Bert needs five cooked shrimp for the night watch.
offer: The night watch eats better than the day watch, and I resent it. Five cooked shrimp, and I will not ask where you got them.

steps.todo: Bring Bert 5 cooked shrimp (Fishing and Cooking).
waiting: Five cooked shrimp. Catch them in the pond, cook them at my range. Do not burn them.

done: Bert counts them. "Five. Good. Have some bread. I mean it."

quests.name: Leather for the Barracks
quests.summary: Joan needs soft leather for new guard caps.
offer: The guard wears out caps like some people wear out socks. Four pieces of soft leather. Snare rabbits in the meadow south-west of the wall.

steps.todo: Bring Joan 4 soft leather (Hunting).
waiting: Four soft leather. Kit Ferris will sell you a snare.

done: Joan turns the leather in the light. "Supple. You have a good eye. Keep the cap."

quests.name: Imps on the Road
quests.summary: Hob says the moss imps have got bold.
offer: The imps have started biting carts. Eight of them. Not a hero's job, just a job.

steps.todo: Defeat eight moss imps.
waiting: Eight moss imps. Along the south road and in the trees.

done: Hob nods. "The road is quieter. Thank you."

quests.name: Glow in the Dark
quests.summary: Sergeant Maud wants the glowcap crawlers thinned out.
offer: Crawlers. Poison on every bite. Six of them, farther out than the imps. Bring a shield and some food.

steps.todo: Defeat six glowcap crawlers.
waiting: Six glowcap crawlers. They poison on a hit; eat before you start.

done: Maud grunts. "Not bad for a Wanderer. You may report to the yard whenever you want a drink of water."

quests.name: Gnashers on the Road
quests.summary: The Warden wants the gnashers cleared from the road beyond the Reach.
offer: The gnashers have taken the far road. They come in packs of three. Bring armor, bring food, and do not go alone if you can help it. You can't, I know. Go anyway.

steps.todo: Defeat three gnashers.
waiting: Three gnashers. They are in the far corners of the Reach.

done: Osric clasps your arm. "The Reach is yours for now. Wait until you see the Moors."

quests.name: The Mind Goblin
quests.summary: Wren wants the goblins cleared from the warren and their leader put down.
offer: The warren mouth is north of the pines. Four of the pinegrubs first, so the rest learn to be careful. Then we talk about their leader.

steps.todo: Defeat four pinegrub goblins.
waiting: Four pinegrub goblins. They keep to the hall and the western den.

steps.todo: Defeat the Mind Goblin.
say: Good. Now the big one. He sits in the chamber at the back, behind the middle den. Eat before you go in, and do not count on running.
waiting: The Mind Goblin is in the back chamber. Bring food.

done: Wren laughs, tired and relieved. "Quiet at last. The pines will grow back. Keep whatever he dropped."

quests.name: The Drainage Cut
quests.summary: Foreman Marrow needs timber and ore for the drainage cut.
offer: The cut is not holding. I need birch for the shoring, six logs, and iron ore for the pins. Cut the birch in Alderwood, west of the water. Your forestry has to be level 10.

steps.todo: Bring six birch logs to Marrow.
waiting: Six birch logs. Alderwood is west of the cut.

steps.todo: Bring four iron ore to Marrow.
say: Good timber. Now the ore for the pins: four iron. Ironback Rocks are east of the village. A level 10 pick.
waiting: Four iron ore. East of the village, in the Ironback Rocks.

done: Marrow slaps the last pin into the timber with the flat of her hand. "That will hold until the next flood. Which is Tuesday."

quests.name: A Crew Below
quests.summary: Lenny wants proof of what happened to the second shift.
offer: The crew kept notes. Tally slips, shift marks, a line or two to their families. The things down there carry them still, in their pockets, in their nests. Bring me three. Then I will know.

steps.todo: Find three crew notes in the Delve and the Downs.
waiting: Three crew notes. The rats, the bats and the wretches carry them.

done: Lenny reads each slip twice and puts them away, one by one, inside his coat. "They were trying to climb out. The water was faster. Thank you."

quests.name: Rats in the Stores
quests.summary: Peg wants the sump rats cleared out of the ore store.
offer: Eight sump rats, as many as you can find on the Downs or in the Delve. They come in threes, so bring something that does not die from three bites.

steps.todo: Defeat eight sump rats.
waiting: Eight sump rats. They run in packs of three.

done: Peg counts the sacks twice. "Whole. First time in a month. Take this and do not tell Ray I paid you."

quests.name: Iron for the Smith
quests.summary: Ray needs four iron bars, smelted by hand.
offer: Four iron bars. You dig the ore, you smelt it at my furnace, one ore a bar. Smithing level 10. If you cannot smelt, learn on bronze and come back.

steps.todo: Bring four iron bars to Ray.
waiting: Four iron bars. Ore from Ironback Rocks, smelted at the furnace.

done: Ray turns a bar over in the tongs and nods. "Even. Clean. You will do."

quests.name: The Foreman Below
quests.summary: Marrow needs to know what became of her brother, the old foreman.
offer: Lenny told me what you found. My brother is still down there. What is left of him throws picks at anything that moves.
The Delve is south of the village, down the road. Go through the galleries to the chamber at the bottom. You cannot run from him once it starts.

steps.todo: Defeat the Foreman Below in the Delve of the Black Sump.
waiting: The Foreman is in the chamber at the bottom of the Delve. Bring food.

done: Marrow stands very still for a long time. "Thank you. I will tell the village he was a good foreman. That is true as far as it goes."

quests.name: A Catch for the Harbor
quests.summary: The harbormaster needs trout for the quay crews.
offer: The crews have eaten nothing but bread for a week. Fish, good fish, from the piers. Trout will do. Six of them, raw, and I will see you paid.
Dan has the rods. Fish the south piers.

steps.todo: Bring six raw trout to Harbormaster Eli.
waiting: Six raw trout. They bite near the shore on an ash rod.

done: Eli counts them twice and writes in the ledger. It is the first honest entry the book has seen all month.

quests.name: The Maid at the Salt Lantern
quests.summary: Aelwyn wants to hit something. The dune boars will do.
offer: The boars in the dunes keep eating the tavern garden. I would go myself but Tess says I would be missed.
I would like you to hit five of them. Hard. Hard enough that I feel it from here.

steps.todo: Defeat five stone boars in the dunes east of Gullsend.
waiting: Five boars. They are in the dunes, east of the city.

done: Aelwyn listens, nods once, and for the first time that day stops carrying plates. "Better. Thank you. I will remember this when it matters."

quests.name: Bow Practice
quests.summary: Dame Rhoda wants you to shoot four gnashers on the road.
offer: Words teach nothing. Four gnashers on the road verge. Shoot them from range if you have a bow, and if you do not, go and buy one.

steps.todo: Defeat four gnashers along the road with any weapon, a bow by preference.
waiting: Four gnashers on the road verge. Keep your distance.

done: "Four. Good. You flinched less each time." Rhoda sets a hand on your shoulder for exactly one second.

quests.name: Supper for the Quay
quests.summary: Bill wants five cooked trout for the quay crews.
offer: The crews are hungry and the range is free. Five trout, properly cooked, and I will pay you well.

steps.todo: Bring five cooked trout to Bill Hale.
waiting: Five cooked trout. Catch them, then use the range.

done: Bill tastes one and goes quiet. "Perfect. Do not tell the others I said so."

quests.name: Lights on the Dunes
quests.summary: Eli wants the blue lights on the dunes put out.
offer: There are lights on the dunes after dark. Blue, low, and moving the wrong way. The crews say they are hounds, and that they follow the boats in.
Put out five. I do not care how. I care that they stop.

steps.todo: Defeat five wisp hounds on the dunes east of Gullsend.
waiting: Five wisp hounds. They run the dunes east of the city at night.

done: Eli takes the report without looking up. "Good. Now the dunes are only dark. I can work with dark."

quests.name: A Wolf at the Door
quests.summary: Rhoda wants the dire wolves west of the city thinned.
offer: The wolves came down from the hills this autumn. Too still, too quiet, always looking the wrong way. They took a net-mender last week.
Four of them. Keep your range. If one closes, you have already lost the exchange. Then make it a different exchange.

steps.todo: Defeat four dire wolves in the west woods.
waiting: Four dire wolves in the west woods. Do not let them close.

done: Rhoda looks at the pelts a long time. "Shadow-touched. Burn them. Do not keep a scrap." Then, quieter, "Well shot."

quests.name: The Wolf-Moon's Fever
quests.summary: Warden Leofric wants the sick wolves put down and the source found.
offer: Wolves are dying wrong, and the hunters blame each other. Kill six that have gone mad, and you will see what I mean.
Then find the pack-lord. He is in the cairns, with something wrong in his eyes.

steps.todo: Defeat six grave wolves on the moors.
waiting: Six grave wolves. They run the moors south of the lodge.

steps.todo: Defeat Greymuzzle the Pack-Lord in the Nameless Cairns.
waiting: Greymuzzle leads the pack in the cairns, south of the lodge.

done: The Warden looks at the pelt, then at you. "It was not hunger. It was a leash. Well done."

quests.name: The Bone Mask
quests.summary: Morwenna Pickman sits in the heart of the cairns. End her.
offer: The feeding came from her. She talks pleasantly the whole time, and she means every word. End it.

steps.todo: Defeat Morwenna Pickman in the Nameless Cairns.
waiting: She sits at the bottom of the cairns, past the warden Ethelgar.

done: Leofric turns the mask over and does not touch it. "Bone. Her kind keep the Seal in bone. Take it with you. Please do not leave it here."

quests.name: Grave Dust
quests.summary: Dot wants five measures of grave dust for the smokehouse seal.
offer: I have a use for dust from the old dead. The kind that stays on the shoes. Five measures, from the wights.

steps.todo: Bring five grave dust to Dot Fell.
waiting: Five grave dust. Barrow wights in the cairns carry it.

done: Dot sniffs it and wrinkles her nose. "Yes. That is the stuff. No, do not ask what for."

quests.name: Lamps Upon the Mere
quests.summary: Moll wants trout for the lamp oil, then the Tide Matron dealt with.
offer: The lamps burn trout oil. Eight, raw, and I will keep them lit.
Then go down the causeway. Something under the water has been fishing back, and she is the one holding the line.

steps.todo: Bring eight raw trout to Moll Lowe.
waiting: Eight raw trout. Fish off the deck edge in Marwick.

steps.todo: Defeat Nyth-Ael, the Tide Matron, in the Drowned Hall.
waiting: Nyth-Ael keeps the gallery of the Drowned Hall, down the causeway south of the village.

done: Moll sets the lamp down and lets the light flicker. "She kept the eels. They are leaderless now, and angry. But fewer. Take the rod. It was meant for you."

quests.name: Eel Trouble
quests.summary: Toby wants five eels off the shallows around the village.
offer: The eels have been through every net I own. Thin them out. Five, on the shore.

steps.todo: Defeat five mere eels near Marwick.
waiting: Five eels. They keep to the shallows on the shore.

done: Toby counts his nets and finds all of them whole for the first time in weeks. "Good. Do not tell them where the nets are."

quests.name: The Drowned Prince
quests.summary: Prince Elrenor offers terms to everyone who comes. Refuse him.
offer: I took him across once. He asked me to wait. I did not. Go and finish what I left him in.

steps.todo: Defeat Prince Elrenor the Drowned in the Drowned Hall.
waiting: He waits in the chamber at the far end of the Drowned Hall. He will offer terms. Say no.

done: Hal looks at the water for a long time. "He is quiet. First time in eighty years. I will row out tonight and see if the lake is the same."

quests.name: The Hermit's Supper
quests.summary: Nick the Hermit wants three cooked rabbit and offers a crystal in return.
offer: I have not had a hot supper since the autumn. Three rabbit, cooked, and I will see you do not leave empty-handed.

steps.todo: Bring Nick 3 cooked rabbit (Hunting and Cooking).
waiting: Three cooked rabbit. Snare them, cook them, and do not tell the goat.

done: Nick eats the first rabbit in two bites and the second in one. "Splendid. I have been living on pine nuts and spite."
He presses a blue crystal into your hand. "Found it in a stream. It hums at the wrong pitch. You may as well have it."

hpregen.label: health per round in a fight

manaregen.label: mana per round in a fight

trees.name: Slash
trees.blurb: Strike the foe in front of you.

trees.name: Multi Strike
trees.blurb: Hit up to four foes in front of you.

trees.name: War Cry
trees.blurb: Boost your damage for a few rounds.

trees.name: Backstep
trees.blurb: Run away from the nearest foe.

trees.name: Deadeye
trees.blurb: Your next shot hits for 350% and always crits.

trees.name: Ice Storm
trees.blurb: Frost over an area, slowing foes.

trees.name: Mana Shield
trees.blurb: Mana takes damage before you do.

trees.name: Arcane Surge
trees.blurb: Your spells hit much harder for a few rounds.

trees.name: Elemental Attunement
trees.blurb: Spells ignore 1% of armor per rank.

trees.name: Meteor
trees.blurb: A huge blast on an area.

trees.name: Summon Familiar
trees.blurb: A familiar fights beside you for the rest of the battle. Casting again heals it.

trees.name: Shield Bash
trees.blurb: Bash the foe and stagger it.

trees.name: Fortify
trees.blurb: Take less damage for a long while.

trees.name: Stoneskin
trees.blurb: Absorb damage for a couple of rounds.

trees.name: Unbreakable
trees.blurb: You cannot fall for two rounds.
